transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because things have been... a little complicated at work. I'm a computer support specialist, and, well, I don't want to sound like a difficult employee or anything, because I really do try to do my best and get along with everyone. But for over a year now, I've been trying to get someone to take it seriously that... well, the new ticket rotation and the security audits, I think they're being used to build a paper trail against me. 

Management keeps showing me the system logs and saying it's just standard policy, and I always try to be agreeable with them, I really do, but... it just doesn't feel right. I just want someone to listen to my side of it. I hope that makes sense? Am I explaining that okay?

When management shows you the system logs and explains it's standard policy, does that ever change your mind at all, even a little, or do you remain completely certain that they're building a case against you regardless of what evidence they show you?

Well, I... I really try to keep an open mind, Dr. Smith. I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn or difficult. When they sit me down and show me the logs, I always look at them carefully, and I nod, and I tell them I understand the policy. I really do want to believe them and just get back to work. 

But... um... I hope this doesn't make me sound unreasonable, but no, it doesn't really change my mind. 

Deep down, I just know what I'm seeing. Even with the logs they show me, I can see exactly how the audits and the ticket rotations are being set up to build that paper trail. I've been watching this happen for over a year now, and... well, I just can't ignore it, even though I really, really want to just be a good team player. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to be completely honest with you about it.

Aside from what's happening at work, do you find yourself generally suspicious of other people's motives in your personal relationships—like with friends or family—or is this feeling that people are against you specific to this situation with your employer?

Oh, no, not at all! I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm, you know, paranoid about everyone. I promise I'm not like that. 

My relationships with my family and my friends are wonderful. I trust them completely. I've been married for thirty years, and I have a great relationship with my kids. I don't ever worry about their motives or think they're out to get me. 

It's really just... just this one specific thing at work. I've always gotten along with everyone everywhere else in my life. I always try to be helpful and kind to people. So it's just the situation at the office that has me so stressed out. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure you know I'm not, um, a suspicious person by nature. I really try to see the best in people.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never experienced anything like that. I really want to assure you, Dr. Smith, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, and my heart goes out to them, but my mind is very clear. 

I'm just a regular guy who goes to work, does his best, and comes home to his family. I hope you believe me? I really want to be as helpful and accurate as possible for you. I promise I'm not keeping anything like that from you.

Aside from the stress and worry this is causing you, has this belief affected your ability to actually do your job well or get along with your coworkers day-to-day, or have you been able to keep performing your work and daily routine largely as before?

Well, I... I really try to keep everything as normal as possible. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, you know? I still do my job, and I'm still polite to everyone. I always make sure to say good morning and ask about their weekends. 

But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I want to be honest with you—it has affected things a little bit. Not a lot! Just... well, I've started asking to be taken off certain network projects. Just the ones where I feel like the audits are being used against me. And, um, I spend a lot more time writing up my ticket notes now. I just want to make sure I'm documenting everything perfectly, so there's no misunderstanding about my work. 

I think... I think maybe it's made some of the team meetings a little tense, and I know I'm probably taking longer to finish things because I'm being so careful. I really hate that it's slowing down the collaboration with the rest of the group. I always prided myself on being a fast worker. 

Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm a bad employee because of it. I'm really just trying to protect myself so I can keep doing a good job for them. Is it normal to react that way when you're under this kind of stress?
